significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a "small set of attention heads is causally responsible" for preserving an agent-specific stale state, while "separate world-tracking heads" support the current state—a form-(ii) causal decomposition rather than a mere existence claim or quantitative law. It establishes both a selective behavioral phenomenon—false-belief performance collapses while true-belief tracking is spared—and a mechanism that fixes explanations for two task classes through independently manipulable belief- and world-state circuitry; this is more constraining than the behavioral deficits catalogued by ToMi (Le et al., 2019) and FANToM (Kim et al., 2023). Verified false would determinately reject the proposed compact, head-level dissociation, although it would not distinguish distributed circuitry from other alternatives, so the negative branch is useful but not decisive. In the topic-substitution check, replacing this specific two-circuit causal claim with generic "research on LLM beliefs" would not justify the score, whereas the quoted opposite ablation effects are false of the topic-median representation-and-probe hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handle is the candidate "false-belief heads," usable as an ablation target, together with probes for the "true current location" and "agent-attributed location"; these are chiefly post-hoc diagnostic and attribution tools, since the claim does not say they forecast failures before an answer or provide a performance-improving intervention. After re-extraction on a new model, the conclusion supplies a procedure for finding possible heads but no ordering, scaling law, threshold, or other relation predicting what the new model will contain. The firm hypothesis concerns first-order false-belief behavior, while non-spatial and second-order transfer is only something "we further test whether"; downstream uptake therefore primarily belongs to mechanistic-interpretability and theory-of-mind researchers rather than model auditors or deployment practitioners. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the generic beliefs topic supplies neither the quoted head-level handle nor its selective ablation target, but the claim-specific deliverable still has roughly the reach of a calibrated, post-hoc circuit probe.
